name: Today's Report
headline: Mortgage rates answer to the bond market more than the Fed, and today's 7.48% adds $2,375 a month to the local median home compared with 3%.
teaser: The 3% mortgage versus today's 7.48% on a local median home, the Fed's first hike since 2023, and why mortgage rates follow the bond market.

sections.label: Real estate
sections.html:
Debt, and what it does to rates. This Sunday's big money story is Ray Dalio's warning about government and corporate debt. The federal debt passed $40 trillion on Aug. 18 and stood at $40.31 trillion on Oct. 8, per the Treasury. For a home buyer, the part that matters is the mortgage rate: Mortgage News Daily's 30-year fixed is 7.48% and the 15-year 7.15%, Friday's readings, with the 30-year up 1.10 points in a year.

The 3% math, done right. One widely read newsletter put the cost of a $400,000 loan at about $975 a month more than at 3%. The real gap is larger: $1,686 at 3% against $2,791 at today's 7.48%, or $1,105 more. Their figure is the gap at 7.00%.

On a local home. The median list price across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City is $1,074,950. With 20% down, that is $3,626 a month at 3% and $6,001 today: $2,375 more, or about $28,500 a year. That gap is why so many owners with low rates stay put, which keeps listings thin.

What it means for you. Waiting for 3% is a plan; it just isn't a schedule. Even at 6%, the median payment would be $845 lower than today, so if you are buying, a refinance later is a realistic hope, not a promise. If you are selling, price against today's payment, not last spring's.

Today's count. Board wide: 2,662 listings across the 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 154 coming soon and 236 brand new. The five city ledger carries 684 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City, 611 on the market and 73 coming soon, down from 688.

Fremont holds 239 live listings: 195 active, 26 coming soon and 18 brand new, with a median on market list price of $1,275,000 at $797 a square foot and a typical listing out 33 days. Hayward carries 192, Milpitas 100, Newark 91 and Union City 62. Across all five cities the median is $1,074,950 at $676 a square foot, 288 homes are priced under a million, and 148 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

images.alt: Bar chart of the monthly principal and interest on $1,074,950, the median list price in Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City, with 20% down: $3,626 at 3%, $4,106 at 4%, $4,616 at 5%, $5,156 at 6% and $6,001 at today's 7.48%, a gap of $2,375 a month.
images.caption: At 3%, the median local home cost $3,626 a month in principal and interest. At today's 7.48%, it is $6,001.

sections.label: Economy
sections.html:
The Fed moved once. The Fed raised its target range to 3.75% to 4% on Sept. 17, its first hike since July 2023, with inflation at 3.4% in August. Mortgage rates did not wait: Freddie Mac's weekly 30-year rose from 5.98% on Feb. 26 to 7.40% on Oct. 8, while the Fed moved a quarter point. Mortgages follow the 10-Year Treasury, which closed Friday at 5.24%. The Fed gets the headlines; the bond market sends the bill.

Metals. Gold settled Friday at $4,216.30, up 1.43%, silver at $61.05, up 2.73%, and Brent at $104.72, up 0.42%.

images.alt: Line chart from January 2015 to October 8, 2026 of the Fed's target range and Freddie Mac's weekly 30-year fixed mortgage rate. The Fed raised its range to 3.75% to 4% on Sept. 17, 2026, its first hike since 2023, while the 30-year rose from 5.98% on Feb. 26 to 7.40% on Oct. 8.
images.caption: The Fed's one hike this year came Sept. 17. By that week the 30-year had already climbed from 5.98% in February to 6.95%, and it has reached 7.40% since.

sections.label: Stocks
sections.html: Closed for the weekend. The numbers above are Friday's close, when all three averages rose and finished the week higher. The S&P 500 is up 14.1% this year and the Nasdaq 17.7%. Monday is Columbus Day: stocks trade, the bond market does not. Earnings season starts Tuesday with JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Citigroup and Johnson & Johnson.
